$comment: Recorded assistive-technology sessions. A11y-3, per ADR-025.
THE EVIDENCE IS MANUAL AND THE GATE IS MECHANICAL. Nothing here can be
generated: A11y-3 is a person sitting down with NVDA or VoiceOver and
reporting what it actually said, which is the whole reason the level exists.
axe and the browser-observed specs already agree the accessible tree is
correct; what they cannot observe is announcement order, verbosity, and how a
virtual cursor traverses.
JSON, NOT YAML. The plan record said yaml. No YAML parser is installed, and
the machine-read files in this directory -- state.json, performance-
budgets.json -- are JSON already. Adding a dependency so one file could use a
different syntax is not a trade this needed.
KEYED BY CONTRACT AND interactionRevision, because that is what invalidates a
session. `contractVersion` moves when props change and a screen reader could
not care; `interaction.revision` moves when keyboard, focus or ARIA behaviour
changes, which is exactly when a recorded session stops describing the
component. Evidence at a revision below the contract's is stale, and the gate
treats it as absent rather than as partial credit.
WHO IS GATED was derived from `interaction.profile` in the component registry
and never listed here. THAT DERIVATION NO LONGER EXISTS: the registry was
deleted in ae4e294 and the CLI that printed the verdict on 2026-09-03 (ADR-031,
Migration step 4). Under ADR-031 a component's accessibility contract is the
table beside it; which components owe a recorded session is decided when a
contract table declares a profile, and until one does this file cannot say.
`sessions` is EMPTY, and that is the honest state rather than an oversight:
no component has ever had a recorded session. The gate that read this file
went with the verification gate in a3cf31b; whatever replaces it reads
`ledgerFailures` in `packages/design/policy/interaction/assistive-technology.mjs`,
which remains and is the one implementation of the verdict.
A session records the tool and its version because 'tested with a screen
reader' is not evidence -- NVDA with Chrome and VoiceOver with Safari
disagree, and which pair was used decides what the result means.
AND THAT SENTENCE IS NOW ENFORCED, which it was not when it was written. The
gate read `interactionRevision` and nothing else, so `{"interactionRevision":
1}` was a pass -- no reader, no version, no date, no tester, nothing announced.
The prose above and ADR-025 both promised more, and agreed with each other
rather than with the code.
`packages/design/policy/interaction/assistive-technology.mjs` is the schema;
ADR-030 is the decision; `tests/unit/at-session.test.ts` shows it the shapes it
must refuse. The schema lived in `tooling/verify/lib/at-session.mjs` until it
moved beside the `interaction.profile` declarations that decide who is gated;
the tooling copy is deleted, per ADR-024.
THE SHAPE, so nobody has to read the validator to record a session:
"Dialog": {
"interactionRevision": 1,
"runs": [{
"at":      { "name": "NVDA", "version": "2024.4" },
"browser": { "name": "Chrome", "version": "131" },
"os": "Windows 11",
"tester": "who sat down with it",
"scenarios": [{
"name": "opening moves focus to the first field",
"announced": "WHAT IT SAID, verbatim -- not 'pass'"
TWO PAIRINGS ARE REQUIRED: NVDA + Chrome and JAWS + Chrome. One reader cannot
tell a component defect from a reader quirk. VoiceOver + Safari is NOT required
and that is recorded exposure, not an oversight -- it needs macOS hardware this
project does not have, and a gate nobody can satisfy is one that gets waived.
